customManagers.description: The KCL module each Composition pulls at render time. Bumping these was hand work: notice the module published, edit the pin, bump meta.crossplane.io/version, fix the README table, open the PR. Renovate does the noticing and the typing; verify still decides whether it may land — since dagger v0.122.0 it also validates the rendered status against the XRD, which is the failure class an automated module bump would otherwise carry onto a cluster.

packageRules.description: Our own KCL modules, one PR each. NOT grouped: a module bump is a behaviour change with its own reasoning, and today's chains showed why the reasoning matters — a catalog version that needs a newer platform to publish what it reads is a decision, not a routine update.
